jobs.title: Director, Blockchain Platform Architect – Technology Incubation – R&D
jobs.description:
Your opportunity

At Schwab, you’re empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us “challenge the status quo” and transform the finance industry together.

We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

The Schwab Technology Services (STS) Research & Development team explores emerging technologies and turns them into practical capabilities that create measurable value across Schwab. We operate at the intersection of innovation and execution—rapidly testing ideas, partnering across the enterprise, and scaling what works.

The Blockchain Platform Architect will define and guide the architecture for enterprise-grade blockchain and digital asset platforms within the Technology Incubation organization. Reporting to the Director of Technology, this role will translate emerging blockchain opportunities into secure, scalable, and operationally resilient platform designs that can move from experimentation to enterprise adoption.

This architect will partner closely with engineering, cloud, security, enterprise architecture, risk, legal, compliance, product, and business stakeholders to design platforms that balance innovation speed with Schwab’s standards for security, resiliency, governance, and client trust.

Key Responsibilities

Own the target-state architecture and technical roadmap for blockchain and digital asset platform capabilities, including platform components, service boundaries, integration patterns, APIs, data models, and operational controls.
Design secure, scalable, fault-tolerant distributed systems that support experimentation, pilot delivery, and production use.
Evaluate blockchain protocols, node infrastructure, custody patterns, smart contract frameworks, interoperability models, and blockchain data access strategies.
Partner with engineering teams to guide implementation, review designs, resolve complex technical tradeoffs, and establish reusable platform patterns.
Collaborate with security, risk, legal, compliance, and enterprise architecture teams to ensure platform designs meet enterprise controls, regulatory expectations, defense-in-depth principles, and operational resilience requirements.
Define architecture documentation, reference models, decision records, design standards, and graduation criteria needed to move capabilities from prototype to sustainable ownership.
Serve as a technical advisor to the Director of Technology and executive stakeholders by translating blockchain architecture choices into business value, risk implications, investment needs, and adoption paths.

Success Measures

Blockchain platform initiatives have clear architecture direction, reusable patterns, documented tradeoffs, and measurable progress toward incubation milestones.
Security, risk, compliance, and operational readiness requirements are built into the platform design early rather than added late in the delivery lifecycle.
Engineering teams can move faster through common platform standards, reference architectures, reusable services, and clear decision records.
The Director of Technology and executive stakeholders have clear visibility into platform maturity, technical risks, dependencies, and decisions required for enterprise adoption.

What you have

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical field (advanced degree a plus).
10+ years of experience in software engineering including delivering platforms, or complex technology initiatives.
Strong technical foundation in modern architectures, cloud-native development, and engineering best practices; ability to guide technical decisions without needing to be the primary implementer.
Demonstrated ability to influence across organizational boundaries and collaborate effectively with Product, Risk, Legal/Compliance, Security, and business stakeholders.
Excellent communication skills—able to align leaders, and convey technical tradeoffs clearly.
Deep experience designing and operating enterprise platforms, distributed systems, cloud-native architectures, APIs, event-driven patterns, observability, resiliency, and DevSecOps practices.
Strong understanding of blockchain fundamentals, distributed ledger technologies, consensus mechanisms, cryptography, smart contracts, tokenization concepts, node operations, custody models, and digital asset transaction flows.
Experience applying security and control patterns such as authentication, authorization, encryption, key management, secrets management, secure coding, vulnerability management, monitoring, and incident response readiness.
Ability to work across ambiguous, emerging technology spaces while producing practical architecture artifacts, decision frameworks, and implementation guidance.
Clear communication skills with the ability to influence engineers, architects, product partners, risk stakeholders, and senior leaders.

In addition to the salary range, this role is also eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

Reporting to the Director of Technology, this role will translate emerging blockchain opportunities into secure, scalable, and operationally resilient platform designs that can move from experimentation to enterprise adoption.

Blockchain platform initiatives have clear architecture direction, reusable patterns, documented tradeoffs, and measurable progress toward incubation milestones.
Security, risk, compliance, and operational readiness requirements are built into the platform design early rather than added late in the delivery lifecycle.
Engineering teams can move faster through common platform standards, reference architectures, reusable services, and clear decision records.
The Director of Technology and executive stakeholders have clear visibility into platform maturity, technical risks, dependencies, and decisions required for enterprise adoption.

What you have

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical field (advanced degree a plus).
10+ years of experience in software engineering including delivering platforms, or complex technology initiatives.

Demonstrated ability to influence across organizational boundaries and collaborate effectively with Product, Risk, Legal/Compliance, Security, and business stakeholders.
Excellent communication skills—able to align leaders, and convey technical tradeoffs clearly.
Deep experience designing and operating enterprise platforms, distributed systems, cloud-native architectures, APIs, event-driven patterns, observability, resiliency, and DevSecOps practices.

Experience applying security and control patterns such as authentication, authorization, encryption, key management, secrets management, secure coding, vulnerability management, monitoring, and incident response readiness.

Clear communication skills with the ability to influence engineers, architects, product partners, risk stakeholders, and senior leaders.

jobs.title: Orlando Technology Audit & Advisory Senior Manager
jobs.description:
JOB REQUISITION

Orlando Technology Audit & Advisory Senior Manager

LOCATION

ORLANDO

ADDITIONAL LOCATION(S)

Job Description

You Belong Here

The Protiviti Career provides opportunity to learn, inspire, and advance within a collaborative and inclusive culture. We hire curious individuals for whom learning is a passion. We lean into our mission: We Care. We Collaborate. We Deliver.

At every level, we champion leaders who live our values of integrity, inclusion, innovation, and commitment to success
. Imagining our work as a journey, we believe integrity guides our way, inclusion moves us forward together, innovation creates new destinations, and our commitment to success empowers us to deliver on our vision to be the most trusted global consulting firm.

Where We Need You: 

Protiviti is looking for a Technology Audit & Advisory Senior Manager to join our growing team.

What You Can Expect: 

As a Senior Manager, you’ll partner with our clients to manage risk associated with their use of technology. You'll develop strategies to solve complex business problems using new ways of thinking, and devise solutions to support your clients' needs through analytics, automation or the latest tools and methods.  You’ll develop lasting relationships with client personnel and further these relationships through quality product delivery.  You’ll foster a network within the business community and serve as an ambassador of Protiviti in the market. You will also be a mentor and provide performance development to teams as you oversee the successful completion of project work plans.

At Protiviti, Technology Audit & Advisory Focuses On

Helping clients better manage risks associated with their use of technology, protecting and enhancing enterprise value.
Innovation: identifying solutions to client problems related to technology, helping them to rethink how technology processes are managed by incorporating AI and automation.
Technology enablement: Incorporating analytics, AI, automation and other new tools and methods in the execution of audit work for our clients, enabling a deeper, broader, more efficient, and more insightful analysis of our clients’ technology risks.
Staying current: We support a broad set of potential certifications and related trainings for our team, equipping our technology audit organization to stay at the forefront of emerging risks and trends.

Consultants In Technology Audit & Advisory Work With Clients To Assess, Identify Risk, Advise, And Consult On Different Technology-related Topics, Including

Cybersecurity
Cloud Assurance
Project Risk Advisory
Technology Risk Management and Assessment
IT General Controls (ITGC)
AI and Data Governance
Data Privacy
Technology Regulations
Enterprise Applications
Technology Resilience
IT Sarbanes-Oxley Compliance
Emerging Technologies
2nd Line Controls Governance
Technology Enablement

What Will Help You Be Successful: 

You enjoy identifying areas of business and technology risk, and opportunities to improve efficiency, increase performance, and help clients better utilize all technologies. 
You are motivated to learn and interested in all things related to data and technology, including the latest trends and developments. 
You are passionate about building relationships with clients and providing exceptional experiences.
You have an inherent interest in project management and team leadership.
You promote a positive team culture that fosters open communication among all engagement team members. 
You create development opportunities for others, including participating in the creation and rollout of training, and ways for your team to improve our clients and communities.
You have interest in contributing to the preparation of client proposals and strategies to win new business.
You excel at identifying opportunities to integrate product solutions and resources to improve client service capabilities.
You have interest in working with a diverse portfolio of clients across multiple industries.
You are versed in leveraging AI to enhance personal productivity as well as internal audit and SOX activities, including planning, fieldwork and reporting.

Do Your Talents Include the Following? 

Demonstrated experience with: 
Leading teams in implementing IT audit methodologies and developing necessary audit deliverables, including process flows, work programs, audit reports, and control summaries.   
Sarbanes-Oxley Act provisions and methodologies for achieving compliance, in particular the technology implications and requirements. 
Commonly used internal control frameworks, including COBIT, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, CIS, ITIL, etc. 
A passion for:
The latest trends and developments in data and technology, including high-growth topics of cybersecurity, cloud, data governance, privacy, analytics, enterprise applications (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Workday, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics etc.), disaster recovery, systems development methodologies etc. 
Analytics and technology enablement (automation, AI/ML etc.). 
Evaluating, summarizing, organizing, and interpreting data.
Establishing and cultivating business relationships and a professional network, including with senior executives. 
Successfully pursuing business development opportunities and identifying and implementing strategies to obtain new work or clientele.
Ability to translate and communicate technology topics and audit issues to client personnel, including executives. 
Leadership and direct supervisory experience of teams including conducting performance appraisals, mentoring and coaching, oversight and review of work, coordination across teams, and understanding how to motivate.  

Your Educational and Professional Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline (e.g., Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or business-related field.)
7+ years working in technology audit, consulting, assurance services, risk and control programs, or related field, either in professional services or industry. 
Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite applications. Secondary emphasis on Vision and Access.
Proficiency in PowerBI, Tableau, Alteryx, Python, RPA Solutions, and other Analytics tools strongly preferred.
Professional Certification such as CIA, CRMA, CISA, CISM, CISSP, or similar strongly preferred.

Our Hybrid Workplace

Protiviti practices a hybrid model, which is a combination of working in person with a purpose and working remotely. This model creates meaningful experiences for our people and our clients while offering a flexible environment. The ratio of remote to in-person requirements varies by client, project, team, and other business factors. Our people work both in-person in local Protiviti offices and on client sites, which can include local or out-of-state travel based on our projects and client requests and commitments.

Protiviti is not registered to hire or employ personnel in the following states – West Virginia, Alaska.

Starting salary is based on a full-time equivalent schedule. Placement in the range is dependent upon experience, skills and geographic work location. Below is the salary range for this job.

$118,000.00 - $189,000.00

Our annual bonus plan provides eligible employees additional cash and/or discretionary stock compensation opportunities. Below is the bonus target opportunity for this job.

14%

The total cash range is estimated from the sum of the base salary range plus the bonus target opportunity. Below is the estimated total cash range for this job.

$134,520.00 - $215,460.00

Employees are eligible for medical, dental, and vision coverages, FSA and HSA healthcare accounts, life and accident insurance, adoption and fertility assistance, paid parental leave up to 10 weeks, and short/long term disability. We offer eligible employees a company 401(k) savings and investment plan with an employer match of 50% on the first 6% of your contributions. We provide Choice Time Off (CTO) for vacation, personal needs, and sick time. The amount of (CTO) varies based on years of service. New hires receive up to 20 days of CTO per calendar year. Protiviti also recognizes up to 11 paid holidays each calendar year.

Learn more about the variety of rewards we offer at Protiviti at https://www.protiviti.com/sites/default/files/2026-01/2026_u.s._benefit_highlights.pdf.

Any benefits outlined are part of our reward offerings for full-time employees in the U.S. Your Open Enrollment materials, insurance contracts, plan documents and Summary Plan Descriptions together comprise the official plan document which legally governs the administration of your benefit plans. Protiviti reserves the right to terminate or amend your benefit plans in any way and at any time.

Protiviti is an Equal Opportunity Employer. M/F/Disability/Veteran

As part of Protiviti’s employment process, any offer of employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check.

Protiviti is committed to being an equal employment employer offering opportunities to all job seekers, including individuals with disabilities. If you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to apply for a position, please contact us by sending an email to HRSolutions@roberthalf.com or call 1.855.744.6947 for assistance.

In Your Email Please Include The Following

The specific accommodation requested to complete the employment application.
The location(s) (city, state) to which you would like to apply.

For positions located in San Francisco, CA: Protiviti will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

For positions located in Los Angeles County, CA: Protiviti will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering & Development
jobs.description:
Overview

SitelogIQ
is a world-class team making a large-scale impact on the efficiency and sustainability of the places we live, work, shop, and heal.

SitelogIQ delivers turnkey solutions across energy efficiency: lighting upgrades
, EV infrastructure
, solar and energy storage system
[distributed generation (DG)] , and other facility improvement measures (FIMs)
that transform built environments and breathe life into the sustainability, financial, and resiliency goals of real estate teams, corporations and public sector organizations across the U.S. Our mission is to make buildings better while making it easy for our clients to accelerate their impact.

Job Summary

The Director of Engineering & Development for Distributed Generation
within our Commercial Markets Division
provides strategic leadership and oversight of the project engineering and development function and team. This role establishes departmental priorities and standards across team management, tools and systems, project scope development, engineering execution, budget estimating, scheduling, quality, risk management, and workflow.

Key Components Of This Role Include

Management: Strategic leadership and management of the DG team, including Project Development Engineers; oversight of resource planning, project priorities, workflows, day-to-day operations, training and mentoring, performance, and continuous improvement.
Project Engineering & Development: Direct, facilitate, and/or review site survey [audit] analysis, conceptual project designs, estimating, schedules, product specifications, code research and application, and the preparation of proposal documents.

An effective SitelogIQ Director of Engineering & Development will partner with leaders across Sales, Operations, and Project Management and represent the team and its technical solutions to clients and their technical staff. They will oversee program and project development milestones to deliver timely, comprehensive proposals that clearly communicate project intentions and solutions while meeting SitelogIQ financial and risk metrics. SitelogIQ team members are expected to share knowledge with others by serving as a constant contributor, trainer, mentor, and resource.

Target Salary:
$145,000 - $180,000 dependent on experience.

Director, Engineering & Development Responsibilities

Provide leadership, direction, coaching, and mentorship to the team as they develop and produce DG project designs and proposals.
Oversee the internal proposal queue, resource allocation, team assignments, risk review process, and client commitments.
Facilitate collaboration between the Engineering & Development and Sales teams to determine customers’ specific technical requirements, project scope, definition of work, and product feature needs.
Establish and maintain quality standards for project designs, submittals, and permitting packages.
Lead the development of new processes, tools, and workflows and the continuous improvement of existing practices.
Partner with Sales to define customers’ technical requirements, project scope, definition of work, and product or system feature needs.
Participate in site-surveys, pre-bid and pre-construction meetings as needed; noting that SitelogIQ’s commercial markets team does have an Assessment team devoted to supporting all types of site-surveys including DG projects.
Maintain all internal documentation in a collaborative file sharing and storage environment.
Lead technical strategy and support for large RFP and business development opportunities.
Participate in quality control review of peer project development team
Ensure effective coordination of installation details with Project Managers and Account Executives and support field installation when needed.
Oversee the evaluation of site audits and selection of product solutions that provide clients with the optimal balance of functionality, long-term operating expense, aesthetics, and constructability.
Establish quality control standards and review submittal packages (product data sheets; bill of materials; standard and customer drawings; layout and connection detail drawings; return on investment analysis; etc.) for content accuracy and alignment with proposal goals.
Review and markup drawings for typical product applications
Review and present DG solution proposals
Ensure local jurisdiction code compliance research is completed and incorporated into project solutions.
Partner with construction leaders to establish accurate project cost estimates.
Establish design intent and specifications and ensure the team consistently meets them.
Provide technical leadership for large RFP and business development opportunities, including the creation of detailed submittal packages.
Coordinate installation details with Project Managers and Account Executives. Support field installation when needed
Lead quality control reviews of projects
Any, and all ad hoc reporting, requests or other tasks deemed

Director, Engineering & Development Requirements & Qualifications

Industry experience and credentials required:
At least 10 years of progressive experience in engineering, project development, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading, managing, and developing a team.

Active Professional Engineer license in at least one U.S. jurisdiction, with the ability to obtain additional licenses through comity as required.
Experience understanding audit and field survey data and translating that into design documents and drawings.
Experience performing sales liaison and client collaboration in energy or related industries.
Strong understanding of DG systems and corresponding customer requirements.
Excellent understanding of financial business principles.
Adept at project scheduling, task definition and effort estimation.
Demonstrated ability to lead projects from concept through completion.
Strong design evaluation, documentation writing skills, problem solving skills, and attention to detail.
Professional communication and presentation skills.
Must be able to work independently, with minimal supervision under time sensitive deadlines.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office products such as Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, etc.
Experience with file sharing, document management and collaboration tools.

Work Environment And Physical Requirements

This position operates in both office and field settings. While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be regularly required to sit, stand, talk, hear, reach, bend, stoop, kneel, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer, phone, and keyboard. May regularly need to lift up to 20 lbs., unassisted. Travel will be required for site assessments and customer presentations.

Benefits

We offer a highly competitive salary, and comprehensive benefits, including:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Disability and life insurance
401K
Flex time off
12 paid holidays
Tuition reimbursement
Opportunities to drive our DE&I efforts by joining our affinity groups, Veterans and Allies Leadership Organization, or Women Inspiring & Strengthening Everyone
Opportunities to give back to our local communities through organized events or fundraisers

More About SitelogIQ

At SitelogIQ, we’re focused on creating a great environment for our team first so that it is more energizing and rewarding to focus on creating great customer experience. That’s what we call a win-win.

We partner with clients in K-12, higher ed, government, healthcare, multifamily housing, and industry to optimize energy efficiency, improve indoor air quality, address lighting, and improve the customer experience. With offices across the country, it’s rewarding to make a difference in the communities where our teammates live and work.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employee may be asked to perform other related duties as required to meet the ongoing needs of the Organization .

SitelogIQ is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in the E-Verify program.

Not Applicable

Employment type

Full-time

Industries

A major responsibility of this position is to bring the Technical Support team to bear to consult on design for strategic as well as plant projects to assure adherence to standards, promote technical strategic direction, and support execution of projects’ technical areas.

This position also provides leadership and direction for technical SMEs and other engineering disciplines, to develop and execute strategies that improve asset reliability, operational availability, and sustainable plant performance. jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Digital Experience
jobs.description:
Job Description

About the Role

Our Digital Experience engineering organization is growing from 16 to more than 21 engineers across multiple squads — including three squads working in a shared codebase — while delivering the most consequential initiatives on our roadmap. We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead this organization through its next stage of growth: its strategy, its processes, its people, and its partnership with Product.
You'll lead through a layer of squad leads who own the day-to-day and performance of their squads (engineers and QA). Your job is to manage, coach, and develop those leads, inspect team-level outcomes, and own the health of the engineering organization as a whole.
The measure of this role is not individual output. It is whether the teams around you deliver faster, more predictably, and with fewer things in their way.
What You'll Own

Engineering Strategy
Be the engineering voice in strategic conversations about what we build and how we build it — participating from the first conversation on new initiatives, not after decisions are made.
Shape how the engineering organization is structured — squad composition, roles, and skill mix — to meet current-year objectives while planning for a multi-year horizon.
Own the point of view on our tech stack and architecture direction: whether what we have today supports where the product is going, and what needs to change before it becomes a constraint.
Partner with Product leadership as a peer when planning future years — Product brings the business perspective, you bring the engineering perspective, and together you organize the squads and the plans.

Engineering Leadership — Process and Tone
Set the process and tone for how engineering runs — the "how" (development and release processes) and the "what" (team functions and responsibilities) — without removing squad independence.
Establish and steward a release process appropriate for an organization of this size: who does what and why, checklists, rollback plans, and cross-team notification.
Define the development process end to end: how PRs move through the system, what the delivery pipeline looks like, how AI is incorporated into engineering work, and what happens when problems arise.
Be the leader engineers look to for expectations. When something isn't clear, work with the leads to make it clear.
Provide stewardship for the squads sharing a codebase as the organization grows — alignment on standards, coordination, and shared ownership.
Bring a clear point of view to Product leadership on what Product should bring to the table for engineering teams to work effectively — and expect the same in return.

Leadership Development & Organizational Health
Manage, coach, and develop the squad leads — your direct reports and the primary lever for everything else.
Build a consistent management practice across squads: how leads run their teams, coach their people, handle performance, and grow their engineers — so an engineer's experience doesn't depend on which squad they're on.
Maintain an accurate talent picture across the organization through the leads: who is growing, who needs support, who is ready for more complex work, and whether people are progressing at the pace we'd expect.
Own engineering throughput at the organizational level: how stories move through development, where they get stuck, and what to change. Find bottlenecks and work with leads to fix them.
Plan capacity and hiring ahead of need as the team scales, so process and staffing don't become the reasons delivery slows down.

Thought Partnership
Come to the table with thinking not just on how tasks get completed, but on how we organize and enable teams to complete them. Removing what's in the teams' way matters more than doing the work yourself.
Be a genuine peer to Product and business leadership — someone who strengthens strategic conversations rather than just executing their outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days:
A clear diagnosis of current delivery bottlenecks with a recommended plan, and established expectations with leads on how teams run.
First year:
Release and development processes that scale to 21+ engineers; throughput measurably improved; a lead layer that is managing well and consistently; a talent picture leadership trusts; engineering fully represented in next-year planning.
Ongoing:
Product and engineering leadership operating like sections of the same orchestra — aligned on expectations in both directions, planning the future together.

Responsibilities and Benefits

What We're Looking For

Experience leading engineering organizations of 15–40 people through a growth phase, ideally with multiple squads in a shared codebase.
Experience managing through a leadership layer — developing leads rather than managing every engineer directly.
A track record of building right-sized process — enough structure to scale, not so much that squads lose independence.
Strong people-management instincts: coaching, performance development, and the judgment to make talent recommendations backed by direct inspection.
Fluency with delivery metrics and workflow data; comfort diagnosing bottlenecks and acting on them.
Strategic range: able to contribute to multi-year product and organizational planning, not just current-quarter execution.
A collaborative operating style with Product — a peer partner, not a service provider.

How You're Supported
As part of the Mission Pet Health family, you get the stability of a local practice backed by the comprehensive benefits and resources of a larger network. The focus is on investing in you, so you can focus on what you love.

Note: Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you at every stage. Eligibility for specific benefits varies based on your role and hours worked.
Competitive Compensation

A competitive hourly rate or salary based on your experience and role.
Health & Wellbeing

We offer comprehensive coverage options including Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance, along with access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for all teammates.
Financial Security

Plan for your future with our 401k retirement options and additional financial protection benefits like Life Insurance and Disability coverage.
Commitment to Growth

We support your career goals with opportunities for professional development, including educational assistance for qualified teammates to enroll in AVMA-accredited veterinary technician programs.
The Power of a Network

About Us

Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Provide clear updates (KPIs, status, metrics) to an executive audience and key stakeholders

Must be open to occasional travel to Fanatics offices and other locations for conferences, events, meetings, and team-building activities

3+ years of experience managing one or more engineering teams
4+ years of experience building highly scalable and fault tolerant systems
You have knowledge of a broad range of design approaches and can deconstruct an architecture to be developed by different teams
Able to scope a project with targeted dates to ensure your team meets business needs
Knows how to discern which features are essential, can be triaged, or omitted and works to negotiate with Product Management
Able to effectively communicate complex technical subjects to a variety of audiences (engineers, technical leaders, marketing and operations teams, non-technical functional leaders)

Excellent analytical and problem solving skills

Thrives in an entrepreneurial, hyper-growth environment where priorities evolve regularly and decisions are made quickly
Team-first mentality, with a willingness to do what it takes to get the job done and a desire to strive for better
Able to effectively work cross-functionally within an enterprise environment

Strong mobile software engineering background
Experience working with Kotlin Multiplatform and/or Compose Multiplatform

jobs.description:
About Futurex

Futurex is a Texas-based leader in hardware security modules (HSMs), enterprise key management, and data protection, trusted by global financial institutions, payment processors, and cloud providers for more than four decades. Futurex Cloud Infrastructure delivers secure, highly available services to customers around the world.

Role overview

The Senior Manager, Site Reliability Engineering - Cloud Infrastructure owns the availability, security, and operational excellence of Futurex Cloud Infrastructure worldwide. You will lead a globally distributed SRE team that runs production infrastructure across multiple regions, cloud providers, and datacenters.

This role sits at the intersection of cloud operations, security, and compliance. Our customers depend on services that cannot go down, so reliability here is measured in customer trust as much as uptime.

You will report to executive leadership and partner closely with Engineering, Product, Security, Compliance, and Customer Support.

Key responsibilities

Team leadership

Lead, hire, and develop a global SRE team across multiple time zones, with clear ownership and follow-the-sun coverage
Own the global on-call program, including rotation design, response time standards, escalation paths, and coverage across all regions
Hold the team accountable for incident response, remediation follow-through, and adherence to operational standards
Set the SRE roadmap, staffing plan, and operating budget

Reliability and service levels

Define and own SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets for Cloud Infrastructure services, and use them to balance stability against release velocity
Partner with Sales and Legal so customer SLA commitments are consistently met
Track SLA compliance and error budget consumption across all services

Operational reporting

Deliver regular reporting to executive leadership on uptime, SLA performance, incident trends, and on-call metrics such as response times and escalation volume
Maintain dashboards that give leadership and stakeholders real-time visibility into service health
Produce customer-facing incident reports and root cause analyses for significant events

Incident management

Own the incident response process, including severity definitions, escalation paths, and customer communications
Lead postmortems and drive remediation items to closure
Serve as the senior escalation point during major incidents

Infrastructure and operations

Review monitoring, observability, and alerting standards
Maintain and regularly test disaster recovery and business continuity plans against defined RTO and RPO targets

Security and compliance

Operate within the controls required by industry security and compliance frameworks
Oversee secure operational procedures, including dual control and chain of custody where required
Enforce strict tenant isolation, least-privilege access, and change management
Support internal and external audits with accurate operational evidence

Requirements

Required qualifications

10+ years in SRE, DevOps, or production infrastructure roles, including 5+ years managing engineering teams
Experience leading geographically distributed teams across multiple time zones
Proven ownership of a production SaaS or cloud platform with contractual SLAs and 24x7 operations
Hands-on depth in at least one major cloud provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure), with working knowledge of the others
Strong background in Linux, networking, infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar), and CI/CD
Experience operating under compliance frameworks such as PCI DSS, SOC 2, or ISO 27001
A track record of building incident management, observability, and DR programs
Clear written and verbal communication with executives, customers, and auditors
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience

Preferred Qualifications

Experience operating security-sensitive or cryptographic infrastructure
Familiarity with security certification standards such as FIPS 140
Experience running hybrid environments that combine public cloud with physical datacenter hardware
Experience leading datacenter migrations or regional expansions
Background in financial services or another highly regulated industry

Benefits

Health, dental, vision, life, and short/long-term disability insurance
Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave
Competitive compensation and opportunities for advancement
Retirement plan with employer contribution match
Welcoming, family-style corporate culture uniquely suited to fast-paced, entrepreneurial, and motivated individuals

Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

The Developer Experience (DevX) team is a high-impact group charged with fueling the future of Crusoe’s engineering muscle. We’re responsible for critical developer tools and infrastructure that are used by all of Crusoe engineering. We focus on accelerating development while ensuring we keep a high bar for quality.

We’re looking for a Senior manager who will own multiple charter’s within DevX, in particular our AI remote agent platform, a suite of standard agents (coding, reviewing, maintenance/upgrades) running on that platform and support for our coding harnesses.

You will play a critical role in shaping our technical direction, communicating a strategic vision, and fostering a company-wide culture of engineering excellence. By partnering with stakeholders across the organization, you will define the future state of Crusoe’s evolving software development efforts and eliminate the friction that stands between an engineer and their "flow state." This is a full-time position for a visionary leader who wants to influence the long-term technical objectives of a company aligning the future of computing with the future of the climate.

What You'll Be Working On:

jobs.description:
Job Description

The Senior Manager – Controls and Automation Software Development
is responsible for leading Patterson-UTI’s Controls and Automation Development team, providing the technical leadership, engineering governance, and organizational capability required to deliver safe, reliable, and scalable drilling control systems across the company’s fleet.

This role is accountable for engineering execution, software development processes, architecture governance, software quality, release management, engineering standards, and the continuous development of a high-performing software engineering organization. The Senior Manager leads a multidisciplinary team responsible for PLC software, HMI applications, simulation, quality assurance, and software platform development.

Working closely with Product Management, Sustaining Engineering, and New Projects teams, this leader ensures engineering execution aligns with business priorities while maintaining the highest standards for software quality, technical excellence, and predictable delivery.

This position reports to the Director, Controls & Automation.

Detailed Description

Engineering Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing Controls Software Engineering organization responsible for delivering safe, reliable, and scalable control software across Patterson-UTI’s drilling fleet.
Establish a culture of technical excellence, accountability, ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Lead Technical Leads, Senior Engineers, Quality Engineering, and third-party engineering resources responsible for software development and validation.
Develop organizational capability through structured coaching, mentorship, succession planning, and leadership development.
Define and maintain engineering career ladders and technical competency expectations across all engineering levels.
Develop and maintain the Principal Engineer pipeline by identifying, mentoring, and growing future technical leaders.
Own workforce planning, future staffing strategy, and hiring plans aligned with the Controls & Automation technology roadmap.
Establish and maintain the technical hiring bar for the organization and participate in final technical interviews for senior engineering positions.
Lead the performance management process, ensuring evaluations are based on measurable performance, technical contribution, leadership, and organizational impact.
Promote a diverse and inclusive work environment where employees feel respected, supported, and empowered to contribute their best work.

Technical Governance

Establish the technical direction for the Controls Software Engineering organization while empowering Technical Leads and Principal Engineers to own detailed solution design and implementation.
Govern software architecture through structured architecture reviews, engineering standards, and technical design processes.
Ensure engineering teams consistently deliver high-quality software, documentation, control algorithms, and system designs that meet company standards.
Own the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), including development standards, coding practices, testing methodologies, documentation requirements, release controls, and change management processes.
Define and enforce software contribution standards, including code quality, modularity, documentation, maintainability, and testability.
Own the engineering technical debt strategy by ensuring technical debt is identified, prioritized, and systematically addressed during release planning.
Maintain active technical engagement across all engineering programs by evaluating architecture proposals, identifying technical risks, facilitating architecture reviews, and resolving escalated technical decisions.
Champion modern software engineering practices including AI-assisted software development, automated testing, simulation, continuous integration, static code analysis, and engineering productivity tools.
Ensure software engineering practices comply with company cybersecurity policies and secure software development lifecycle standards.
Stay current with industrial automation technologies and software engineering best practices to continuously improve engineering capabilities.

Engineering Delivery & Release Excellence

Own engineering execution for the Controls Software Engineering organization, ensuring commitments are delivered safely, predictably, and with high quality.
Drive the department’s platform release cadence by ensuring development across all engineering teams converges into stable, production-ready software releases.
Own engineering planning, release planning, capacity planning, resource allocation, dependency management, and delivery forecasting.
Conduct regular engineering delivery reviews with Technical Leads to identify execution risks, remove organizational blockers, and maintain predictable delivery.
Make engineering Go/No-Go recommendations for software releases in partnership with Quality Engineering and Product Management.
Establish measurable engineering performance metrics and continuously improve engineering effectiveness.
Drive continuous improvement in software quality, engineering productivity, release predictability, and deployment readiness.
Work closely with Product Management during field qualification, beta testing, and release validation to ensure successful deployment of new functionality.
Establish strong communication channels with field operations and technical support organizations to capture operational feedback and continuously improve engineering deliverables.

Engineering Infrastructure & Platform

Own the long-term evolution of Patterson-UTI’s Controls Software Platform, driving modular architecture, software reuse, hardware abstraction, configuration-driven deployment, maintainability, and scalability.
Maintain governance of the company’s software intellectual property and engineering assets in accordance with corporate policies.
Oversee the Controls Engineering Laboratory, simulation environments, software qualification infrastructure, and engineering validation processes.
Ensure engineering teams have the development environments, simulation capabilities, testing frameworks, and engineering tools necessary to deliver high-quality software efficiently.
Lead continuous improvement of software validation, simulation, and qualification processes to reduce engineering risk and improve release quality.

Demonstrated Ability In The Following Leadership Competencies

Builds and Maintains Effective Relationships
Develops Self and Others
Builds Effective Teams
Courageous Leadership
Managing Vision and Purpose
Business Acumen
Drive for Results
Customer Focus
Decision Quality

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, Automation Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent industry experience.
Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience developing industrial controls software, preferably PLC- and HMI-based systems.
Demonstrated experience leading software engineering teams responsible for industrial automation or mission-critical control systems.
Strong understanding of industrial communication protocols.
Demonstrated ability to lead multiple engineering programs while managing competing priorities and delivery schedules.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Fifteen or more years of experience developing industrial control systems within drilling, rig equipment, oil and gas, or other heavy industrial automation industries.
Previous leadership experience managing multidisciplinary software engineering organizations.
Experience with industrial automation platforms such as Omron, Siemens TIA Portal, WinCC, Ignition or equivalent.
Experience with HMI development, simulation environments, automated software testing, and software quality systems.

Experience supporting field commissioning, troubleshooting, and deployment of industrial automation systems.

jobs.title: Hiring Event - Chief Software Engineer V
jobs.description:
Overview

Great minds meet great challenges.

Ready to build what’s next?

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of NSD, combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

Event Details

Our hiring event will take place during the weeks of October 12th to November 13th.

Selected candidates may be invited to participate in virtual and onsite interviews during this timeframe and will be contacted directly with scheduling details.

This role is performed full-time onsite at the PNNL campus in Richland, WA or Seattle, WA.

Responsibilities

With new projects and expanding programs, our AI and Data Analytics Division offers opportunities to advance cutting-edge research and build solutions for critical national security missions. Join a team of more than 400 data scientists, software engineers, mathematicians, and human-centered computing researchers turning ambitious ideas into real-world capabilities.

We're hiring across three complementary chief engineering tracks
, and we're looking for people who want to own something meaningful end-to-end: from the platform beneath it, to the systems that power it, to the experience humans actually touch.

Skills We’re Seeking

DevSecOps and Platform Engineering: Design and build scalable AI platforms, cloud-native infrastructure, containerized environments (Docker/Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, IaC, real-time data stream architectures, and reliable, secure production systems. We are particularly interested in engineers with strong Python expertise and significant experience in DevOps, platform engineering, site reliability engineering, distributed systems, telemetry and observability, security, and automated software delivery.
AI Systems & Data Platform Software Engineers: Push the boundaries of agentic AI systems characterized by autonomy, adaptability, reasoning, collaboration, and effective tool use. We are seeking experienced software engineers and nationally recognized technical leaders who have designed and deployed agentic AI systems and large-scale data platforms in real-world environments. Relevant expertise includes large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, multi-step reasoning, autonomous decision workflows, model and data orchestration, production-quality AI systems, and designing and operating petabyte-scale ETL/ELT pipelines. Senior candidates may also shape research directions, lead multidisciplinary R&D programs, develop external partnerships, and mentor AI scientists and engineers.

Learn more about the PNNL AI and Data Analytics Division.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

PhD and 5 years of relevant experience -OR-
MS/MA and 7 years of relevant experience -OR-
BS/BA and 9 years of relevant experience -OR-
AA and 18 years of relevant experience -OR-
HS/GED and 20 years of relevant experience.
Relevant experience is defined as Software Engineering experience in designing, architecting, programming, deploying, and automating software solutions in support of scientific research or consumer digital product development.

Current, hands-on software development experience using Python.

Hazardous Working Conditions/Environment

Not applicable.

Additional Information

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a federal security clearance.

A security clearance background investigation includes review of your employment, education, financial, and criminal history, as well as interviews with you and your personal references, neighbors, and co-workers to determine trustworthiness, reliability, and loyalty to the United States. The investigation also examines your foreign connections, drug and alcohol use, foreign influence, and overall conduct.

Requirements

U.S. Citizenship
Background Investigation: Applicants selected will be subject to a Federal background investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified matter in accordance with 10 CFR 710, Appendix B.
Drug Testing: All Security Clearance positions are Testing Designated Positions, which means that the applicant selected for hire is subject to pre-employment drug testing, and post-employment random drug testing. In addition, applicants must be able to demonstrate non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for the 12 consecutive months preceding completion of the requisite Questionnaire for National Security Positions (QNSP).

Note: Applicants will be considered ineligible for security clearance processing by the U.S. Department of Energy if non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for 12 months cannot be demonstrated.

“Referral Eligible”

Testing Designated Position

This position is a Testing Designated Position (TDP). The candidate selected for this position will be subject to pre-employment and random drug testing for illegal drugs, including marijuana, consistent with the Controlled Substances Act and the PNNL Workplace Substance Abuse Program.

About PNNL

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Every year, scores of dynamic, driven people come to PNNL to work with renowned researchers on meaningful science, innovations and outcomes for the U.S. Department of Energy and other sponsors; here is your chance to be one of them!

At PNNL, you will find an exciting research environment and excellent benefits including health insurance, and flexible work schedules. PNNL is located in eastern Washington State—the dry side of Washington known for its stellar outdoor recreation and affordable cost of living. The Lab’s campus is only a 45-minute flight (or ~3 hour drive) from Seattle or Portland, and is serviced by the convenient PSC airport, connected to 8 major hubs.

Commitment to Excellence and Equal Employment Opportunity

Our laboratory is committed to fostering a work environment where all individuals are treated with fairness and respect while solving critical challenges in fundamental sciences, national security, and energy resiliency. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. PNNL considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), protected veteran status, and any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local laws.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures and in employment. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at careers@pnnl.gov.

Drug Free Workplace

PNNL is committed to a drug-free workplace supported by Workplace Substance Abuse Program (WSAP) and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs.

If you are offered employment at PNNL, you must pass a drug test prior to commencing employment. PNNL complies with federal law regarding illegal drug use. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug. If you test positive for any illegal controlled substance, including marijuana, your offer of employment will be withdrawn.

Security, Credentialing, And Eligibility Requirements

As a national laboratory, PNNL is responsible for adhering to the Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which require new employees to obtain and maintain a HSPD-12 Personal Identify Verification (PIV) Credential. To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete the applicable tier of federal background investigation post hire and receive a favorable federal adjudication. The tier of federal background investigation will be determined by job duties and national security or public trust responsibilities associated with the job. All tiers of investigation include a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last 1 to 7 years (depending on the applicable tier of investigation). Illegal drug activities include marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

For Foreign National Candidates

If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) Federal risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement thereafter, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment. The tier of federal background investigation required to obtain the PIV credential will be determined by job duties at the time you become eligible for the PIV credential.

Mandatory Requirements

Please be aware that the Department of Energy (DOE) prohibits DOE employees and contractors from having any affiliation with the foreign government of a country DOE has identified as a “country of risk” without explicit approval by DOE and Battelle. If you are offered a position at PNNL and currently have any affiliation with the government of one of these countries, you will be required to disclose this information and recuse yourself of that affiliation or receive approval from DOE and Battelle prior to your first day of employment.

Rockstar Rewards

Employees and their families are offered medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, robust telehealth care options, several mental health benefits, free wellness coaching, health savings account, flexible spending accounts, basic life insurance, disability insurance*, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, tuition assistance, relocation, backup childcare, legal benefits, supplemental parental bonding leave, surrogacy and adoption assistance, and fertility support. Employees are automatically enrolled in our company-funded pension plan* and may enroll in our 401 (k) savings plan with company match*. Employees may accrue up to 120 vacation hours per year and may receive ten paid holidays per year.

Research Associates excluded.
All benefits are dependent upon eligibility.

Click Here For Rockstar Rewards

Starting pay is calculated from the minimum of the pay range and actual placement in the range is determined based on an individual’s relevant job-related skills, qualifications, and experience. This approach is applicable to all positions, with the exception of positions governed by collective bargaining agreements and certain limited-term positions which have specific pay rules.

Our four company values, Care, Integrity, Accountability and Growth Mindset, are reflected in everything that we do here at Barclays Center. From the interview process to employee recognition, we make certain to incorporate the four values.

Key Attributes for Success

To excel in this role, candidates must demonstrate strong technical leadership, sound judgment under live event pressure, effective communication, collaboration, adaptability, proactive problem-solving, and meticulous attention to detail. These attributes are essential to maintaining reliable broadcast infrastructure, supporting complex live events, and partnering effectively with internal teams, visiting production teams, vendors, contractors, and union crews.

Technical Leadership:
Demonstrates strong engineering leadership and the ability to establish priorities, standards, and clear expectations.

Coaches and develops technical staff while balancing daily operations, event coverage, and long-term system needs.
Takes ownership of system reliability and engineering outcomes.
Collaboration & Partnership:
Works effectively with Production, IPTV, IT, event operations, visiting broadcasts, vendors, contractors, and union crews.

Builds trusted relationships and translates technical requirements into practical engineering plans.
Communicates service expectations, limitations, and escalation paths clearly.
Adaptability:
Responds effectively to changing event requirements, technical issues, maintenance windows, and last-minute schedule adjustments.

Maintains composure and sound judgment in dynamic, high-pressure live event environments.
Adjusts priorities to protect event continuity and operational needs.
Effective Communication:
Explains technical decisions, risks, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Communicates during critical incidents to coordinate service restoration and manage operational impacts.
Creates clear documentation, procedures, and standards that support consistent execution.
Proactive Problem-Solving:
Identifies potential reliability issues and develops preventive maintenance, monitoring, redundancy, and recovery strategies.

Uses incident trends and root-cause reviews to drive corrective actions, training, and system improvements.
Approaches complex technical challenges with practical, solutions-oriented thinking.
Operational & Technical Excellence:
Maintains high standards for system performance, configuration, documentation, and event readiness.

Understands complex broadcast, audio, intercom, monitoring, control, and IP-based infrastructure.
Balances reliability, operational requirements, lifecycle planning, and available resources.
Meticulous Attention to Detail:
Ensures accurate signal-flow, cabling, drawings, inventory, access, configuration, and system documentation.

Oversees testing, commissioning, acceptance, and handover with a high level of technical precision.

Position Summary

The Director of Broadcast Engineering leads the reliability, development, and daily upkeep of technical systems and engineering support for the control room and connected production infrastructure at Barclays Center. Reporting to the Senior Director of Facilities Presentation, this position manages the engineering team, establishes technical standards, and aligns staffing, maintenance, and capital planning with event needs. The Director provides hands-on leadership during complex technical issues and partners with Production, IPTV, IT, and external broadcast teams.

Leads the engineering teams which includes but not exclusive to managing, coaching, and evaluating the Video Engineering team and the Audio Engineering team.
Establishes team priorities, delegate tasks, plan event coverage, and coordinate part-time staff, union crews, and contractors.
Coordinates events and partnership needs in addition to working with production leadership, event operations, visiting broadcasts, and other departments to translate show requirements into practical engineering plans, communicates limitations, and establish service and escalation expectations.
Maintains NBA & WNBA requirements through managing NBA HSAN infrastructure, game clock systems, coach’s feeds distribution, locker room infrastructure, official replay systems, player tracking technology, and related game-day technical requirements.
Own broadcast system performance and oversee the SMPTE ST 2110 environment, including Grass Valley Kayenne/K-Frame, Evertz EXE/MAGNUM, DreamCatcher, Dante audio systems, Riedel intercom, QC monitoring, Adder KVM, and signal distribution systems.
Establishes reliability and recovery plans by developing preventive maintenance, monitoring, configuration backups, software and firmware planning, and redundancy testing.
Leads critical technical responses and acts as a key part of senior staff escalation for issues and failures that affect events or game-day operations. Provides on-call support to coordinate service restoration, communicate impacts, ensures root-cause of issues are reviewed that produces corrective actions.
Manages projects, vendors, and resources. Defines project requirements, evaluates vendors, manage approved expenditures, and oversees installation, commissioning, acceptance testing, and handover.
Maintain engineering standards by creating documentation, inventory, access, and configuration standards.
Coordinates broadcast network changes with IT, maintain drawings and procedures, and uses incident trends to prioritize training and system improvements.

CANDIDATE PROFILE: Who You Are

The ideal candidate brings deep broadcast engineering expertise, strong technical leadership, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced live event environment.

Minimum 10 years of broadcast engineering or comparable live production infrastructure experience, including a minimum of three years supervising technical staff and leading engineering projects, maintenance programs, and/or event support.
Demonstrated ability to design, support, and troubleshoot SMPTE ST 2110 systems, including PTP synchronization, multicast traffic, IP addressing, VLANs, network redundancy, and interfaces between IP and SDI systems.
Strong understanding of switchers, routers, replay/playback, cameras, broadcast audio, intercom, tally/control, and monitoring, with working familiarity with lighting interfaces.
Ability to interpret and create engineering/CAD drawings and establish accurate signal-flow, cabling, and system documentation.
Ability to develop budgets, evaluate technical proposals, manage vendors and implementation schedules, and make equipment lifecycle recommendations based on operational needs, reliability, and available resources.
Sound judgment under live event pressure, with the ability to explain technical decisions clearly, resolve competing priorities, train staff, and collaborate with internal partners, visiting production teams, multiple trades, and union crews.
Ability to work flexible schedules as needed to support live events, urgent technical issues, maintenance windows, and last-minute schedule adjustments. The role regularly requires nights, weekends, and holidays, including extended days, late nights, and early mornings, and may include on-call support for time-sensitive technical needs.
You’re a team player, highly motivated, and have an eye for production best practices

Resident Stories That Stay with You: From Henry, who moved into his first-ever home, to Jaci, whose stay at a Wallick community allowed her to achieve homeownership and graduate college, kickstarting her dream career.
Work-Life Balance: Paid time off, including paid parental leave.
Career Growth: Tuition reimbursement, training, professional development, and advancement opportunities within a company that invests in its people.
Employee Owned, Resident Focused: As a 100% employee-owned company, your daily work (supporting our residents) also contributes to your financial future by sharing in our profitability.

What You’ll Do

The Sr Manager Software Engineering leads Build & Automate, Pillar 2 of Wallick's IT operating model, and holds accountability for every decision within it. The pillar owns the automation portfolio, the integration estate that moves operational data across Yardi, Dayforce, Procore, enterprise systems, and the satellite solutions that extend the systems of record, and it holds Wallick's AI agenda as a joint accountability with the Data & Analytics team. The pillar exists so that Wallick can grow without adding people at the same rate: it automates repetitive work, connects the systems so data moves without being rekeyed, and gives business teams controlled tools for configuration and workflow instead of unrestricted direct admin access to the core systems. You will report to the VP of Information Technology and work together with other team members and leaders.
The seat is deliberately a business-technology leader, not a Principal Architect. The role owns outcomes, priorities, and the pillar's accountability. Deep technical authority lives with the Principal Software Engineer — Integrate & Aggregate, the Sr. manager's trusted technical advisor on architecture and engineering calls. The Leader consults the Principal before committing externally, then decides. Both know the seams, and the model works because they are honest.

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor's degree in business, information systems, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
A track record, typically built over eight or more years, in delivering business technology solutions, including at least three years leading a technical team or a portfolio of technical work.
Business acumen and stakeholder engagement: able to represent the pillar at the executive table, negotiate priorities with business leaders, and explain a technical trade-off in business terms.
Portfolio and priority judgment: experience running a backlog of integration, automation, and software work against business outcomes, and holding the line on scope.
Growing technical breadth rather than depth: working literacy in integration patterns, workflow automation, AI and agent tooling, and modern application platforms, with the appetite to keep learning and the comfort to decide with strong technical input from a peer whose judgment you trust.
AI and automation strategic literacy, exercised jointly with the Data & Analytics team: able to see where automation and AI change an operating process and where they do not, and to reach those judgments with a peer rather than alone.
Governance experience: solution architecture approval, change and release management, and application portfolio decisions (rationalization, sunset, and portfolio health).
People leadership: developing engineers at different career stages, including a principal-level advisor and an early-career builder.
Familiarity with the Microsoft cloud ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Azure, Power Platform, Copilot Studio) is strongly preferred. Experience in multifamily housing, senior living, or another regulated operating business is a plus.

Functions And Responsibilities

Pillar Leadership and Portfolio Management

Lead the Build & Automate pillar and its portfolio of integration, automation, AI, and software engineering initiatives, aligned with business roadmaps.
Provide leadership and career development for the Principal Software Engineer, Integrate & Aggregate, and the Software Engineer, Extend.
Partner with the Principal Software Engineer on architecture and technical strategy, leveraging the role’s technical expertise before making external commitments.
Represent the pillar with IT leadership and business stakeholders, coordinating cross-pillar priorities with the Leaders of Business Capabilities and IT Operations & Trust.

Integration, Automation, and AI

Own the strategy, priorities, health, and outcomes of enterprise integrations, including data movement across Yardi, Dayforce, Procore, and other systems, as well as modernization of legacy integrations.
Oversee the integrations and pipelines that deliver operational data to the Data & Analytics platform, in coordination with business data owners, Data & Analytics, and Power & Protect.
Jointly lead the automation and AI portfolio with Data & Analytics, including prioritization, governance, delivery, and measurement of business value.
Co-chair the AI Council, which governs AI policy, platforms, licensing, data access, investment priorities, and value measurement. Escalate unresolved decisions to the SVP of Organizational Effectiveness and Technology.
Move validated concepts from experimentation into scalable, supported enterprise solutions.

Architecture, Governance, and Applications

Own solution architecture for the pillar, with the Principal Software Engineer developing technical patterns and standards for leadership review and approval.
Oversee change and release governance for pillar solutions.
Manage the application portfolio, including the application register, portfolio health, rationalization, and retirement decisions. Commercial license management remains with the Vendor Management Analyst.
Chair the weekly cross-pillar technical council to coordinate standards, dependencies, and technical decisions.

Transformation Program Leadership

Serve as the default leader for major cross-pillar transformation programs with a significant technology build component, subject to assignment by the VP of Information Technology.
Deliver programs with clear scope, priorities, dependencies, and sequencing.
Partner with Partner & Transform from program inception to incorporate stakeholder engagement, change management, and adoption into delivery plans.

Wallick’s Mission & Values

At Wallick Communities, We Believe In Opening Doors To Homes, Opportunity, And Hope For Our Residents, Associates, And Community. Our Core Values Guide Everything We Do
