new_jobs.title: Senior Manager – Controls and Automation Software Development
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The Senior Manager – Controls and Automation Software Development
is responsible for leading Patterson-UTI’s Controls and Automation Development team, providing the technical leadership, engineering governance, and organizational capability required to deliver safe, reliable, and scalable drilling control systems across the company’s fleet.

This role is accountable for engineering execution, software development processes, architecture governance, software quality, release management, engineering standards, and the continuous development of a high-performing software engineering organization. The Senior Manager leads a multidisciplinary team responsible for PLC software, HMI applications, simulation, quality assurance, and software platform development.

Working closely with Product Management, Sustaining Engineering, and New Projects teams, this leader ensures engineering execution aligns with business priorities while maintaining the highest standards for software quality, technical excellence, and predictable delivery.

This position reports to the Director, Controls & Automation.

Detailed Description

Engineering Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing Controls Software Engineering organization responsible for delivering safe, reliable, and scalable control software across Patterson-UTI’s drilling fleet.
Establish a culture of technical excellence, accountability, ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Lead Technical Leads, Senior Engineers, Quality Engineering, and third-party engineering resources responsible for software development and validation.
Develop organizational capability through structured coaching, mentorship, succession planning, and leadership development.
Define and maintain engineering career ladders and technical competency expectations across all engineering levels.
Develop and maintain the Principal Engineer pipeline by identifying, mentoring, and growing future technical leaders.
Own workforce planning, future staffing strategy, and hiring plans aligned with the Controls & Automation technology roadmap.
Establish and maintain the technical hiring bar for the organization and participate in final technical interviews for senior engineering positions.
Lead the performance management process, ensuring evaluations are based on measurable performance, technical contribution, leadership, and organizational impact.
Promote a diverse and inclusive work environment where employees feel respected, supported, and empowered to contribute their best work.

Technical Governance

Establish the technical direction for the Controls Software Engineering organization while empowering Technical Leads and Principal Engineers to own detailed solution design and implementation.
Govern software architecture through structured architecture reviews, engineering standards, and technical design processes.
Ensure engineering teams consistently deliver high-quality software, documentation, control algorithms, and system designs that meet company standards.
Own the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), including development standards, coding practices, testing methodologies, documentation requirements, release controls, and change management processes.
Define and enforce software contribution standards, including code quality, modularity, documentation, maintainability, and testability.
Own the engineering technical debt strategy by ensuring technical debt is identified, prioritized, and systematically addressed during release planning.
Maintain active technical engagement across all engineering programs by evaluating architecture proposals, identifying technical risks, facilitating architecture reviews, and resolving escalated technical decisions.
Champion modern software engineering practices including AI-assisted software development, automated testing, simulation, continuous integration, static code analysis, and engineering productivity tools.
Ensure software engineering practices comply with company cybersecurity policies and secure software development lifecycle standards.
Stay current with industrial automation technologies and software engineering best practices to continuously improve engineering capabilities.

Engineering Delivery & Release Excellence

Own engineering execution for the Controls Software Engineering organization, ensuring commitments are delivered safely, predictably, and with high quality.
Drive the department’s platform release cadence by ensuring development across all engineering teams converges into stable, production-ready software releases.
Own engineering planning, release planning, capacity planning, resource allocation, dependency management, and delivery forecasting.
Conduct regular engineering delivery reviews with Technical Leads to identify execution risks, remove organizational blockers, and maintain predictable delivery.
Make engineering Go/No-Go recommendations for software releases in partnership with Quality Engineering and Product Management.
Establish measurable engineering performance metrics and continuously improve engineering effectiveness.
Drive continuous improvement in software quality, engineering productivity, release predictability, and deployment readiness.
Work closely with Product Management during field qualification, beta testing, and release validation to ensure successful deployment of new functionality.
Establish strong communication channels with field operations and technical support organizations to capture operational feedback and continuously improve engineering deliverables.

Engineering Infrastructure & Platform

Own the long-term evolution of Patterson-UTI’s Controls Software Platform, driving modular architecture, software reuse, hardware abstraction, configuration-driven deployment, maintainability, and scalability.
Maintain governance of the company’s software intellectual property and engineering assets in accordance with corporate policies.
Oversee the Controls Engineering Laboratory, simulation environments, software qualification infrastructure, and engineering validation processes.
Ensure engineering teams have the development environments, simulation capabilities, testing frameworks, and engineering tools necessary to deliver high-quality software efficiently.
Lead continuous improvement of software validation, simulation, and qualification processes to reduce engineering risk and improve release quality.

Demonstrated Ability In The Following Leadership Competencies

Builds and Maintains Effective Relationships
Develops Self and Others
Builds Effective Teams
Courageous Leadership
Managing Vision and Purpose
Business Acumen
Drive for Results
Customer Focus
Decision Quality

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, Automation Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent industry experience.
Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience developing industrial controls software, preferably PLC- and HMI-based systems.
Demonstrated experience leading software engineering teams responsible for industrial automation or mission-critical control systems.
Strong understanding of industrial communication protocols.
Demonstrated ability to lead multiple engineering programs while managing competing priorities and delivery schedules.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Fifteen or more years of experience developing industrial control systems within drilling, rig equipment, oil and gas, or other heavy industrial automation industries.
Previous leadership experience managing multidisciplinary software engineering organizations.
Experience with industrial automation platforms such as Omron, Siemens TIA Portal, WinCC, Ignition or equivalent.
Experience with HMI development, simulation environments, automated software testing, and software quality systems.
Working knowledge of VFD systems, motion control, and industrial networking technologies.
Experience supporting field commissioning, troubleshooting, and deployment of industrial automation systems.

Work Environment

This position requires the person to be able to work in a time sensitive, high visibility role and regularly travel as needed to support business units and to visit work sites. It may also require extended travel to remote locations and/or overnight stay(s) during variable hours. Variable work hours include hours worked on the weekend, on holidays, and hours to travel within and outside of the assigned region. The Engineer must work with an emphasis on planning, multitasking, and prioritization to maximize efficiency of the team. Must be able to work closely with others and manage customer interaction in a professional manner. Ability to safely navigate work sites with occasional walking, climbing, standing, stepping, working at heights, etc., during normal operating conditions (day/night, outdoor hot/cold weather) and while utilizing designated personal protective equipment (PPE). up to 25%

Join Our Team at Barclays Center!

Congratulations on taking the first step toward embarking on an exciting new adventure at Barclays Center! Our focus is YOU!

At Barclays Center, we're more than just a venue – we're a dynamic community driven by a shared passion for creating unforgettable live experiences. We're dedicated to nurturing our team members and empowering them to thrive in an environment where innovation, collaboration, and a love for sports entertainment intersect.

If you're someone who lives and breathes events, fueled by an unwavering passion for creating magic in every moment, then we want you to join us in shaping the future of live entertainment. Come be a part of our vibrant community, where every day offers the chance to inspire, innovate, and make memories that last a lifetime!

Our Company Values

We understand that it is important for you to know what our values are to determine if they align with yours. Our four company values, Care, Integrity, Accountability and Growth Mindset, are reflected in everything that we do here at Barclays Center. From the interview process to employee recognition, we make certain to incorporate the four values.

Key Attributes for Success

To excel in this role, candidates must demonstrate strong technical leadership, sound judgment under live event pressure, effective communication, collaboration, adaptability, proactive problem-solving, and meticulous attention to detail. These attributes are essential to maintaining reliable broadcast infrastructure, supporting complex live events, and partnering effectively with internal teams, visiting production teams, vendors, contractors, and union crews.

Technical Leadership:
Demonstrates strong engineering leadership and the ability to establish priorities, standards, and clear expectations.

Coaches and develops technical staff while balancing daily operations, event coverage, and long-term system needs.
Takes ownership of system reliability and engineering outcomes.
Collaboration & Partnership:
Works effectively with Production, IPTV, IT, event operations, visiting broadcasts, vendors, contractors, and union crews.

Builds trusted relationships and translates technical requirements into practical engineering plans.
Communicates service expectations, limitations, and escalation paths clearly.
Adaptability:
Responds effectively to changing event requirements, technical issues, maintenance windows, and last-minute schedule adjustments.

Maintains composure and sound judgment in dynamic, high-pressure live event environments.
Adjusts priorities to protect event continuity and operational needs.
Effective Communication:
Explains technical decisions, risks, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Communicates during critical incidents to coordinate service restoration and manage operational impacts.
Creates clear documentation, procedures, and standards that support consistent execution.
Proactive Problem-Solving:
Identifies potential reliability issues and develops preventive maintenance, monitoring, redundancy, and recovery strategies.

Uses incident trends and root-cause reviews to drive corrective actions, training, and system improvements.
Approaches complex technical challenges with practical, solutions-oriented thinking.
Operational & Technical Excellence:
Maintains high standards for system performance, configuration, documentation, and event readiness.

Understands complex broadcast, audio, intercom, monitoring, control, and IP-based infrastructure.
Balances reliability, operational requirements, lifecycle planning, and available resources.
Meticulous Attention to Detail:
Ensures accurate signal-flow, cabling, drawings, inventory, access, configuration, and system documentation.

Oversees testing, commissioning, acceptance, and handover with a high level of technical precision.

Position Summary

The Director of Broadcast Engineering leads the reliability, development, and daily upkeep of technical systems and engineering support for the control room and connected production infrastructure at Barclays Center. Reporting to the Senior Director of Facilities Presentation, this position manages the engineering team, establishes technical standards, and aligns staffing, maintenance, and capital planning with event needs. The Director provides hands-on leadership during complex technical issues and partners with Production, IPTV, IT, and external broadcast teams.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: What You Will Do

Leads the engineering teams which includes but not exclusive to managing, coaching, and evaluating the Video Engineering team and the Audio Engineering team.
Establishes team priorities, delegate tasks, plan event coverage, and coordinate part-time staff, union crews, and contractors.
Coordinates events and partnership needs in addition to working with production leadership, event operations, visiting broadcasts, and other departments to translate show requirements into practical engineering plans, communicates limitations, and establish service and escalation expectations.
Maintains NBA & WNBA requirements through managing NBA HSAN infrastructure, game clock systems, coach’s feeds distribution, locker room infrastructure, official replay systems, player tracking technology, and related game-day technical requirements.
Own broadcast system performance and oversee the SMPTE ST 2110 environment, including Grass Valley Kayenne/K-Frame, Evertz EXE/MAGNUM, DreamCatcher, Dante audio systems, Riedel intercom, QC monitoring, Adder KVM, and signal distribution systems.
Establishes reliability and recovery plans by developing preventive maintenance, monitoring, configuration backups, software and firmware planning, and redundancy testing.
Leads critical technical responses and acts as a key part of senior staff escalation for issues and failures that affect events or game-day operations. Provides on-call support to coordinate service restoration, communicate impacts, ensures root-cause of issues are reviewed that produces corrective actions.
Manages projects, vendors, and resources. Defines project requirements, evaluates vendors, manage approved expenditures, and oversees installation, commissioning, acceptance testing, and handover.
Maintain engineering standards by creating documentation, inventory, access, and configuration standards.
Coordinates broadcast network changes with IT, maintain drawings and procedures, and uses incident trends to prioritize training and system improvements.

CANDIDATE PROFILE: Who You Are

The ideal candidate brings deep broadcast engineering expertise, strong technical leadership, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced live event environment.

Minimum 10 years of broadcast engineering or comparable live production infrastructure experience, including a minimum of three years supervising technical staff and leading engineering projects, maintenance programs, and/or event support.
Demonstrated ability to design, support, and troubleshoot SMPTE ST 2110 systems, including PTP synchronization, multicast traffic, IP addressing, VLANs, network redundancy, and interfaces between IP and SDI systems.
Strong understanding of switchers, routers, replay/playback, cameras, broadcast audio, intercom, tally/control, and monitoring, with working familiarity with lighting interfaces.
Ability to interpret and create engineering/CAD drawings and establish accurate signal-flow, cabling, and system documentation.
Ability to develop budgets, evaluate technical proposals, manage vendors and implementation schedules, and make equipment lifecycle recommendations based on operational needs, reliability, and available resources.
Sound judgment under live event pressure, with the ability to explain technical decisions clearly, resolve competing priorities, train staff, and collaborate with internal partners, visiting production teams, multiple trades, and union crews.
Ability to work flexible schedules as needed to support live events, urgent technical issues, maintenance windows, and last-minute schedule adjustments. The role regularly requires nights, weekends, and holidays, including extended days, late nights, and early mornings, and may include on-call support for time-sensitive technical needs.
You’re a team player, highly motivated, and have an eye for production best practices
You’re self-starter, works well independently, and collaborates in a team environment

KEY COMPETENCIES: Skills You Possess

Troubleshooting, Root-Cause Analysis & Continuous Improvement
Preventive Maintenance, Redundancy & Lifecycle Planning
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Communication
Project, Vendor & Resource Management
Broadcast Infrastructure, Signal Flow & System Documentation
Live Event Systems Reliability & Critical Incident Response
Technical Leadership & Team Development
Broadcast Engineering & SMPTE ST 2110

WORK ENVIRONMENT: Where You Will Be

This position is fully on-site based in Barclays Center, located in the heart of Brooklyn, New York.
This role requires consistent attendance to support daily operations, foster collaboration, and provide direct support to employees, business partners and key stakeholders.
Ability to work flexible hours to support live events, urgent technical issues, maintenance windows, and last-minute schedule adjustments is crucial. Schedules often include nights, weekends, holidays, long days, late nights, and early mornings, with on-call support as needed.

Make a Difference—And Own Your Future

Join Wallick Communities, a 100% employee-owned company with over 55 years of experience in providing affordable housing and assisted living for families and seniors across the Midwest. With 1,000+ associates and a mission to open doors to homes, opportunity, and hope, we take pride in fostering a supportive and collaborative work environment where every employee-owner plays a vital role.

A Career with Wallick Means. . .

Creating Homes for People Who Need It Most: Providing new beginnings for residents seeking affordable, safe and high-quality housing where they can thrive.
Pay-on-Demand: access your money as you earn it.
Exceptional Benefit Package: Health, dental, vision insurance effective within 2 weeks of starting your new job, paid time off, gym membership reimbursement, paid parental leave, 401K, and more!
Work-Life Balance: Paid time off, including paid parental leave.
Learning & Support: A supportive team that cares about your continued development, well-being and professional growth.
Resident Stories That Stay with You: From Henry, who moved into his first-ever home, to Jaci, whose stay at a Wallick community allowed her to achieve homeownership and graduate college, kickstarting her dream career.
Work-Life Balance: Paid time off, including paid parental leave.
Career Growth: Tuition reimbursement, training, professional development, and advancement opportunities within a company that invests in its people.
Employee Owned, Resident Focused: As a 100% employee-owned company, your daily work (supporting our residents) also contributes to your financial future by sharing in our profitability.

What You’ll Do

The Sr Manager Software Engineering leads Build & Automate, Pillar 2 of Wallick's IT operating model, and holds accountability for every decision within it. The pillar owns the automation portfolio, the integration estate that moves operational data across Yardi, Dayforce, Procore, enterprise systems, and the satellite solutions that extend the systems of record, and it holds Wallick's AI agenda as a joint accountability with the Data & Analytics team. The pillar exists so that Wallick can grow without adding people at the same rate: it automates repetitive work, connects the systems so data moves without being rekeyed, and gives business teams controlled tools for configuration and workflow instead of unrestricted direct admin access to the core systems. You will report to the VP of Information Technology and work together with other team members and leaders.
The seat is deliberately a business-technology leader, not a Principal Architect. The role owns outcomes, priorities, and the pillar's accountability. Deep technical authority lives with the Principal Software Engineer — Integrate & Aggregate, the Sr. manager's trusted technical advisor on architecture and engineering calls. The Leader consults the Principal before committing externally, then decides. Both know the seams, and the model works because they are honest.

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor's degree in business, information systems, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
A track record, typically built over eight or more years, in delivering business technology solutions, including at least three years leading a technical team or a portfolio of technical work.
Business acumen and stakeholder engagement: able to represent the pillar at the executive table, negotiate priorities with business leaders, and explain a technical trade-off in business terms.
Portfolio and priority judgment: experience running a backlog of integration, automation, and software work against business outcomes, and holding the line on scope.
Growing technical breadth rather than depth: working literacy in integration patterns, workflow automation, AI and agent tooling, and modern application platforms, with the appetite to keep learning and the comfort to decide with strong technical input from a peer whose judgment you trust.
AI and automation strategic literacy, exercised jointly with the Data & Analytics team: able to see where automation and AI change an operating process and where they do not, and to reach those judgments with a peer rather than alone.
Governance experience: solution architecture approval, change and release management, and application portfolio decisions (rationalization, sunset, and portfolio health).
People leadership: developing engineers at different career stages, including a principal-level advisor and an early-career builder.
Familiarity with the Microsoft cloud ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Azure, Power Platform, Copilot Studio) is strongly preferred. Experience in multifamily housing, senior living, or another regulated operating business is a plus.

Functions And Responsibilities

Pillar Leadership and Portfolio Management

Lead the Build & Automate pillar and its portfolio of integration, automation, AI, and software engineering initiatives, aligned with business roadmaps.
Provide leadership and career development for the Principal Software Engineer, Integrate & Aggregate, and the Software Engineer, Extend.
Partner with the Principal Software Engineer on architecture and technical strategy, leveraging the role’s technical expertise before making external commitments.
Represent the pillar with IT leadership and business stakeholders, coordinating cross-pillar priorities with the Leaders of Business Capabilities and IT Operations & Trust.

Integration, Automation, and AI

Own the strategy, priorities, health, and outcomes of enterprise integrations, including data movement across Yardi, Dayforce, Procore, and other systems, as well as modernization of legacy integrations.
Oversee the integrations and pipelines that deliver operational data to the Data & Analytics platform, in coordination with business data owners, Data & Analytics, and Power & Protect.
Jointly lead the automation and AI portfolio with Data & Analytics, including prioritization, governance, delivery, and measurement of business value.
Co-chair the AI Council, which governs AI policy, platforms, licensing, data access, investment priorities, and value measurement. Escalate unresolved decisions to the SVP of Organizational Effectiveness and Technology.
Move validated concepts from experimentation into scalable, supported enterprise solutions.

Architecture, Governance, and Applications

Own solution architecture for the pillar, with the Principal Software Engineer developing technical patterns and standards for leadership review and approval.
Oversee change and release governance for pillar solutions.
Manage the application portfolio, including the application register, portfolio health, rationalization, and retirement decisions. Commercial license management remains with the Vendor Management Analyst.
Chair the weekly cross-pillar technical council to coordinate standards, dependencies, and technical decisions.

Transformation Program Leadership

Serve as the default leader for major cross-pillar transformation programs with a significant technology build component, subject to assignment by the VP of Information Technology.
Deliver programs with clear scope, priorities, dependencies, and sequencing.
Partner with Partner & Transform from program inception to incorporate stakeholder engagement, change management, and adoption into delivery plans.

Wallick’s Mission & Values

At Wallick Communities, We Believe In Opening Doors To Homes, Opportunity, And Hope For Our Residents, Associates, And Community. Our Core Values Guide Everything We Do

Care – We show compassion and respect for everyone.
Character – We do the right thing, even when no one is looking.

For nearly 60 years, it has been at the core of our organization’s culture that all Wallick associates come to a safe and inclusive place to work. Implement rigorous evaluation, testing, and LLMOps practices — offline benchmarks, regression suites, groundedness and hallucination measures, CI/CD, versioning, observability, tracing, incident response, and rollback.
Engineer secure, permission-aware solutions that enforce identity, entitlements, data boundaries, privacy, human approvals, audit logging, and responsible AI policies.
Define model and platform integration patterns, including model selection and routing, structured outputs, caching, rate limiting, fallback strategies, token budgets, circuit-breaker controls, and cost management.
Partner with cloud, platform, data, and security teams, and with the GenAI Program Manager, to integrate GenAI services with enterprise systems and translate business needs into governed, high-value capabilities.
Lead, coach, and grow a high-performing, multidisciplinary team of GenAI, software, platform, and quality engineers, setting clear expectations, career paths, and a culture of ownership and experimentation.
Manage engineering and product-quality outcomes — availability, latency, throughput, task completion, adoption, developer productivity, and cost per successful outcome.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience (advanced degree preferred).
Proven experience architecting and delivering production GenAI or AI/ML systems at enterprise scale, with recent hands-on coding experience.
Strong proficiency in modern cloud-native engineering (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or Java; APIs, microservices, containers, distributed systems, CI/CD, IaC).
Hands-on knowledge of LLM application patterns — prompting, RAG, embeddings, vector search, orchestration, tool calling, agents, structured outputs, and model evaluation.

OCI combines the speed, ownership, and innovation of a startup with the scale, reliability, and customer focus of one of the world’s leading technology companies.

Oracle Managed Kubernetes (OMK) is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's (OCI) enterprise-grade Kubernetes service that provides a managed, scalable, and secure environment to deploy containerized applications. It is built on the open-source Kubernetes engine and designed to simplify operations, improve performance, and provide deep integration with the broader OCI ecosystem.

We are seeking an experienced hands-on senior engineering manager to manage and grow a team of highly talented engineers responsible for designing, building, and operating software systems for OMK. You will own delivery, architecture, reliability, and operational health across multiple software areas while developing strong engineering leaders and technical talent.

The ideal candidate is an experienced engineering leader with a strong background in distributed systems, cloud services, operational platforms, and people leadership. You are comfortable operating in ambiguous, high-scale environments, driving technical strategy, building durable teams, and partnering across engineering, product, operations, and infrastructure organizations to deliver measurable business impact.

This is an opportunity to lead teams building software that directly improves how OCI supports global data center infrastructure, reduces operational friction, increases automation, and enables OCI to scale efficiently.

Manages the execution of processes to develop and guide new software features and enhancements following design specifications, ensuring accessibility, and to develop documents to clarify software design and code.

Acts as a role model for teams to advocate for customers' interests and suggests product enhancements based on feedback.

Practices and Standards Compliance - Security and Compliance:

Collaborates with teams and other stakeholders within and outside of group to establish, follow, and enforce documented security criteria, development industry best practices and processes, and coding standards.
Ensures clarity of teams' operational objectives for adherence to broad acceptance criteria.
Implements moderately complex secure software development practices requiring information gathering and analysis to prevent security vulnerabilities.

Development Operations - System Maintenance:

Leads teams in performing periodic maintenance and testing operations for systems that require upgrading or patching (e.g., for critical vulnerabilities).
Delegates assignments to teams to implement and evolve standard operating procedures (SOP) for development and for driving improvements, ensuring automation, testing, and debugging of systems to ensure service/product availability, health, support, and reliability.

Planning & Execution:

Manages multiple medium- to large-scale projects or initiatives across teams, ensuring timelines, deliverables, and budgets when applicable are monitored and met. Provides direction to teams on project work, setting priorities, and aligning with business needs. Guides teams on adjusting plans to accommodate resource or timeline changes.

Drives cross-functional partnerships to align expectations and shared objectives across multiple teams. Coaches team members to develop strategic relationships with business leaders, stakeholders, and external partners to foster collaboration and long-term success. Problem Solving:

Provides direction to multiple teams on addressing complex operational and/or technical issues as well as providing guidance on analyzing complex data and/or information to identify solutions. Continuous Learning:

Identifies skill gaps across teams, and empowers team members to pursue learning and knowledge sharing opportunities that build their expertise in new areas and coaches them to apply learnings to advance the organization.

Drives team to collaborate on, develop, and implement ideas to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within and across teams, providing oversight. new_jobs.description:
At Utility, we’re reimagining what’s possible.
Our breakthrough H2Gen® technology transforms undesirable industrial by-products into clean energy and sustainable fuels and feedstocks, helping hard-to-abate industries decarbonize without compromise. We’re building systems and solutions that will power a zero-carbon future by turning what the world doesn’t want into clean energy it needs most.
But technology alone doesn’t change the world.
People do.

We’re building a team as bold as our mission. Engineers and scientists, designers and operators, storytellers and strategists all united by a shared belief: that the undesirable can become invaluable, and that industrial decarbonization can be both practical and economical.
At Utility, we see possibilities where others see limits. We believe progress happens when diverse minds collaborate toward a cleaner, smarter, more resilient world.
If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career, join us and help build what’s next.
The Company

Utility Global
is redefining how the world makes and uses energy. Through its breakthrough H₂Gen® technology
, Utility transforms industrial off-gases and biogases into clean energy and sustainable fuels and feedstocks, helping industries decarbonize without compromise
. The company’s proprietary technology delivers a scalable, economic pathway to a zero-carbon future, positioning Utility as a leader in the industrial decarbonization revolution.
The Role

Utility Global is seeking a strategic, hands-on Director, Ceramic Technology
to lead our Applied Technology ceramic development team in Englewood, Colorado. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this leader will set priorities, guide technical strategy, and develop the people, processes, and roadmap needed to advance ceramic materials and manufacturing technologies for high-temperature reactor components.
The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in ceramic materials and processing with proven experience leading technical teams in fast-paced R&D, pilot-scale, or manufacturing environments. This person should be comfortable translating business and technology objectives into a clear team strategy, making disciplined tradeoffs, mentoring engineers and scientists, and ensuring experimental work leads to actionable decisions and scalable process improvements.
This is a technical leadership role with accountability for both forward-looking ceramic technology development and practical manufacturing readiness. Experience in electrochemical systems is welcome, but strong leadership in ceramic materials, processing, characterization, scale-up, and technology transfer is more important than electrochemistry domain knowledge for this position.

Key Responsibilities

Lead, manage, and develop a team responsible for ceramic materials, bodies, coatings, and processes for high-temperature reactor components.
Set technical priorities, allocate resources, and translate company objectives into a focused ceramic technology roadmap.
Define and guide experimental strategy to improve performance, durability, manufacturability, quality, and cost.
Oversee the translation of bench-scale ceramic development into robust pilot-scale and manufacturing-relevant processes.
Build decision-making frameworks for powder handling, mixing, dispersion, rheology, forming, drying, thermal treatment, inspection, and related process steps.
Partner cross-functionally with R&D, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and external partners to select, evaluate, and qualify ceramic materials and processes.
Establish clear technical standards for testing, characterization, data analysis, documentation, and design reviews.
Guide troubleshooting and root-cause investigations for process and equipment issues affecting quality, yield, consistency, and throughput.
Support technology transfer and manufacturing readiness internally and with third-party production partners.
Communicate strategy, progress, risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to the CTO, leadership team, technical colleagues, and external stakeholders.
Ensure team activities are conducted safely and in compliance with internal procedures and relevant standards.

This role will focus primarily on building and leading a forward-looking ceramic technology function, with ongoing accountability for manufacturing support, technology transfer, and scale-up readiness across both in-house and third-party production.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

BS in Ceramic Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
8+ years of relevant industrial experience, including demonstrated leadership of technical teams; advanced degree preferred.
Proven experience leading ceramic materials, processing, manufacturing development, or scale-up programs in an industrial environment.
Demonstrated ability to manage, coach, and develop engineers, scientists, technicians, or cross-functional technical contributors.
Hands-on familiarity with ceramic processing methods such as extrusion, slip casting, spray coating, isostatic pressing, tape casting, dip coating, gel casting, or related forming and coating processes.
Strong working knowledge of relevant characterization techniques such as dilatometry, rheometry, particle size analysis, SEM, XRD, BET, porosimetry, TGA/DSC, mechanical testing, fractography, or digital image analysis.
Experience applying DOE, statistical methods, root-cause analysis, process qualification, or similar tools to guide technical decisions and process improvement.
Ability to communicate complex technical strategy, risks, and recommendations clearly to executive leadership and technical teams.
Ability to lead effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional R&D environment with evolving priorities and high ambiguity.

Preferred Qualifications:

MS or PhD in Ceramic Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field.
Prior ownership of a ceramic technology roadmap, platform development program, or multi-year scale-up initiative.
Experience transferring technology from R&D into pilot-scale, internal manufacturing, or third-party manufacturing environments.
Prior experience in aerospace, defense, structural ceramics, refractories, filtration, catalyst supports, thermal management, nuclear materials, or other advanced ceramic manufacturing environments.
Experience establishing technical governance, design review processes, quality gates, or process qualification methods for complex hardware or materials systems.
Familiarity with high-temperature reactor systems, harsh-environment oxide materials, or electrochemical devices.

$200,000 - $250,000 a year

What Will Help Someone Succeed in This Role

A leader who can balance strategic direction with practical engagement in technical details, equipment, data, and team problem-solving.
A disciplined, quantitative mindset that turns ambiguous technical problems into clear priorities, experiments, and decisions.
The ability to build structure without creating bureaucracy, especially in an environment where processes are still being developed, refined, and scaled.
A collaborative leadership style that aligns R&D, manufacturing, external partners, and executive leadership around the highest-impact technical work.

Partner with service leadership to define, document, and continuously improve global service business processes, standards, and best practices.
Translate business needs and user experiences into clear system requirements and scalable technical solutions that support the long-term growth of the service business.

Design, manage, and enhance integrations between Salesforce, SAP, internally developed service applications, reporting platforms, and other business systems.
Develop and execute a service master data strategy, ensuring data integrity, governance, consistency, and accessibility across systems.
Build, maintain, and continuously improve dashboards, reports, and KPI frameworks that enable data-driven decision making and provide leaders with clear visibility into business performance.

Act as a trusted partner to Service, IT, Commercial Operations, Finance, Quality, and Field Service teams, building strong relationships and aligning stakeholders around shared business objectives.
Provide technical guidance and business context to IT and development teams, helping prioritize enhancements, solve complex challenges, and identify opportunities for innovation.
Promote consistency and operational excellence by driving adoption of global processes, systems, and reporting methodologies across the organization.
Develop training materials, user documentation, and support programs that empower users and enable successful adoption of systems and tools.
Evaluate emerging technologies and analytics capabilities, proactively identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, visibility, and the overall customer experience.
Take ownership of strategic initiatives from concept through implementation, driving measurable outcomes through collaboration, influence, and continuous improvement.
Help shape the future of the Service Systems, Infrastructure & Analytics function by contributing to team development, process maturity, and long-term organizational success.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Information Systems, or a related field.
7+ years of experience in business systems, analytics, systems architecture, service operations technology, or related disciplines.
Experience supporting field service, technical service, customer support, or equipment-based service organizations.
Strong experience with enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, SAP, Power BI, Tableau, and related business systems.
Proven experience designing system integrations, APIs, data flows, reporting frameworks, and business process automation.
Experience developing dashboards, KPIs, and analytics solutions that support operational and strategic decision-making.
Strong understanding of data architecture, master data management, data governance, and data quality best practices.
Working knowledge of SQL, Python, Power Query, DAX, Power Automate, C#, HTML, or similar scripting and automation tools.
Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions and measurable business outcomes.
Proven success leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing stakeholders across Service, IT, Commercial Operations, Finance, and Quality organizations.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with a customer-focused mindset and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Our mission is to inspire advances in bioprocessing as a trusted partner in the production of biologic drugs that improve human health worldwide.
